messages.content: Write a post about what a software company learned from a year of remote work. Around 250 words.

output:
# A Year Remote: What We Got Wrong

We closed the office in March. Everyone was excited. Then July happened, and half the engineering team quietly stopped showing up to anything that wasn't a standup.

Here's what a year taught us.

**Async isn't free.** We assumed writing things down would replace meetings. It replaced *some* meetings, and added about forty minutes a day of reading. Our design docs grew from two pages to nine. Nobody read page four. We now cap proposals at 800 words and require a "decision needed by" line at the top, and review time dropped by roughly half.

**The onboarding failure was brutal.** Of six people hired remotely in the first six months, four told us in their 90-day check-in that they had no idea who to ask about anything. In the office they'd have overheard it. We assigned each new hire two named humans — one for code, one for everything else — and the complaint stopped.

**Time zones cost more than we budgeted.** A five-hour spread between Lisbon and Chicago sounds workable. In practice it gave us a three-hour overlap, and every unplanned question turned into a next-day question. We stopped hiring outside a four-hour band. That was unpopular and we're still doing it.

**Some things improved and we can't take credit.** Deep work went up. Sick days went down. Our best writer got promoted because writing suddenly mattered.

We're not going back. We also won't pretend the first six months weren't a mess.

---

250 words. The specifics (dates, headcounts, the Lisbon/Chicago spread) are invented placeholders — swap in your real numbers, since the piece leans on them for credibility.
